title: Hypothesis Generation and Semantic Attribution in Inverse Perturbation Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2611.29055v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding gene regulatory relationships at scale can help identify intervention points and anticipate unintended effects, but connecting a black-box model's learned computation to biological knowledge remains difficult. We investigate whether a sparse, typed gene network can generate inspectable hypotheses for steering malignant transcriptional programs toward expression patterns associated with favorable prognosis. Using LINCS L1000 CRISPR/Cas9 profiles paired with matched plate controls, we train a graph neural network to recover the perturbed gene from baseline and endpoint expression. translated_title: 逆向扰动建模中的假设生成与语义归因
translated_abstract: 大规模理解基因调控关系有助于识别干预靶点并预判意外的生物学效应，但将黑盒模型学习到的计算过程与生物学知识联系起来仍然十分困难。我们研究了一个稀疏的、带类型标注的基因网络能否生成可检验的假设，以引导恶性转录程序转向与良好预后相关的表达模式。利用LINCS L1000 CRISPR/Cas9扰动图谱并配对匹配的平板对照，我们训练了一个图神经网络，从基线表达和扰动后终点表达中恢复被扰动的基因。网络节点结合了ProTrek衍生的蛋白质表征与表达特征；边则编码带符号的调控关系及其他基因间相互作用。我们利用这种逆向建模方法，在指定的癌细胞背景下为期望的多基因表达变化提名候选干预措施，并沿从基线到扰动状态的路径使用积分梯度和电导方法进行语义归因分析。
tldr: 该论文提出一种结合稀疏类型化基因网络与图神经网络的逆向扰动建模方法，通过积分梯度与电导等语义归因技术生成可解释的干预假设，为在特定癌细胞背景下实现期望的多基因表达变化提名候选基因靶点。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an inverse perturbation modeling approach combining a sparse, typed gene network with a graph neural network, using semantic attribution techniques (integrated gradients and conductance) to generate inspectable hypotheses and nominate intervention targets for desired multigene expression changes in specified cancer-cell contexts.
